 Digital Foundry says GTA VI's CPU demands make a 40 FPS mode on PS5 Pro too difficult
 Digital Foundry says GTA VI's CPU-heavy world keeps PS5 Pro at 30 FPS, as a 40 FPS mode would require major optimization or cutbacks.
 VIEW GALLERY - 3 This GTA VI store scene illustrates the detailed world that Digital Foundry says puts heavy demands on the CPU, making a 40 FPS mode on PS5 Pro difficult. Hassam Nasir Senior Tech Reporter Published Nov 17, 2026 2:20 PM CST 1 minute & 15 seconds read time What you need to know
 Digital Foundry says GTA VI's dense, CPU-heavy world keeps current-gen consoles, including PS5 Pro, at 30 FPS; its processor is only modestly faster than base PS5. A 40 FPS mode would need optimization or cutbacks, while Pro's gains focus on PSSR clarity and ray-traced shadows.

GTA VI is locked to 30 FPS on every current-gen console, including the PS5 Pro, and Digital Foundry has explained why the rumored 40 FPS middle ground did not happen.

 On a recent DF Direct Weekly, Richard Leadbetter walked through the frame-time math. Rockstar's frame-rate target was confirmed less than a week before launch, so the question had been hanging over the game for some time.
 Read more : Rockstar confirms GTA 6 targets 30 FPS on PS5 Pro with PSSR and ray-traced shadows 
 Read more : GTA 6 may be locked at 30 FPS even on a PS5 Pro, says analyst 
 Read more : GTA 6 deemed 'the single most visually striking game of the generation' by tech experts 
 At 30 FPS, the game has 33.3 milliseconds per frame to simulate its entire world, including traffic, crowds, physics, and the systemic chaos GTA VI runs on. A 60 FPS mode would halve that to around 16.7ms, which Leadbetter called "not viable." The 40 FPS mode fans keep asking for sits at 25ms. That sounds like a modest compromise, but he said it would still demand "a huge amount of optimization or cutbacks" to reach.
 3 GTA VI's traffic-filled streets illustrate the dense world that Digital Foundry says makes a 40 FPS mode difficult on PS5 Pro. VIEW GALLERY - 3 IMAGES The problem is the CPU, not the GPU. GTA VI is CPU-bound because its world is so dense and systemic, and the PS5 Pro's processor is only modestly faster than the one in the base PS5. So the Pro cannot simply brute-force its way past the limit.
 In a game where "literally anything can happen because of the systemic nature of the experience," Leadbetter said chasing lower frame times is "just asking for trouble," and concluded that "30fps makes sense."
 3 GTA VI's busy waterfront scene illustrates the dense world simulation Digital Foundry says makes a 40 FPS mode difficult on PS5 Pro. The PS5 Pro's edge is visual rather than smoother. Rockstar says the Pro gets improved clarity through PSSR and ray-traced shadows the base console does not, all at the same 30 FPS cap. Digital Foundry measured the base PS5 at roughly 1440p internally using footage from the Extended Look, so the Pro's upscaling could sharpen things further. Digital Foundry has argued since the first trailer that the Pro would be a visual upgrade, not a performance one.
 Story Q&A
 Powered by TweakBot
 From TweakTown's coverage of this story.
 Which CPU-heavy parts of GTA VI's world make a 40 FPS mode difficult to achieve on PS5 Pro?
 Traffic, crowds and NPCs, physics, and the game's other interacting world systems all add to GTA VI's CPU workload. Digital Foundry says a 40 FPS mode would leave just 25 milliseconds to simulate that world each frame, down from 33.3 milliseconds at 30 FPS, requiring major optimization or cutbacks. What gameplay or visual tradeoffs might GTA VI need to reach 40 FPS on PS5 Pro?
 To reach 40 FPS, GTA VI would have only 25 milliseconds per frame instead of 33.3, so Digital Foundry says it would need major optimization or cutbacks. The most relevant gameplay tradeoffs would be reducing CPU-heavy world simulation, such as traffic, crowds, physics, or other systems, though no specific cutbacks have been announced. Lowering visual quality alone would not solve the bottleneck, because the limiting factor is the CPU rather than the PS5 Pro's GPU. How does GTA VI look different on PS5 Pro compared with base PS5 at the same 30 FPS cap?
 At the same 30 FPS cap, GTA VI on PS5 Pro gets PSSR for improved image clarity and ray-traced shadows that the base PS5 does not have. Digital Foundry estimated the base PS5 was rendering at roughly 1440p from Extended Look footage, but Rockstar has not disclosed either version's rendering resolution, so there is no confirmed resolution comparison. How does PSSR improve GTA VI's image clarity on PS5 Pro, and is the game using PSSR 2?
 On PS5 Pro, PSSR improves GTA VI's clarity by using machine learning to reconstruct a sharper image from a lower internal rendering resolution, as explained in the separate story "Rockstar confirms GTA 6 targets 30 FPS on PS5 Pro with PSSR and ray-traced shadows." Rockstar confirmed PSSR support, but not PSSR 2. "GTA 6 preload gives up clues that it'll come with a new PSSR 2 version, and that PS5 Pro game could get a 40 FPS mode" reported a possibility based on preload clues, not confirmation that the game uses PSSR 2. Rockstar could still patch in a performance mode later, but the argument is difficult to dismiss. The density players will be staring at is the same density that pins the frame counter at 30. As Digital Foundry sees it, that is a deliberate trade GTA VI made for the most detailed open world Rockstar has built.
